decision_metrics.false_safe_definition: predicted SAFE while actual class is CAUTION or UNSAFE
decision_metrics.false_unsafe_definition: predicted UNSAFE while actual class is SAFE

experiment.scientific_question: Can one fixed low-mid-frequency chirp reliably estimate task-relevant interaction properties and classify whether sustained contact is safe, without requiring accurate separate estimates of k, c, and m_eff?
experiment.title: Stage 1 decision-sufficient interaction identification

combined_task.description: stiffness plus frequency-response and time-domain features; excludes estimated c and m_eff

frequency_response.description: causal force-to-displacement spectral gain, peak, centroid, phase, and band ratios

time_domain.description: causal probe displacement/velocity/acceleration, persistence, gain, and work features

future_contact_maneuver.description: Raised-cosine load to 2 N, sustained hold, raised-cosine unload, and free ringdown. The predictor never receives this response for validation cases.

kill_criterion.rule: Stop and reconsider the probing architecture if the primary combined-task outcome-bound predictor violates any false-safe, accuracy, unsafe-recall, or conservative-bound criterion on untouched validation cases.

risk_envelope.class_rule: SAFE only if every response metric is inside the safe envelope; UNSAFE if any metric exceeds the unsafe envelope or tracking travel; CAUTION otherwise.

safe_force_definition.definition: Disturbance-limited force obtained by linear scaling of the hidden 2 N maneuver response to the safe displacement, velocity, and absolute oscillation envelopes. It does not claim that reduced force fixes slow relative settling.

scope_exclusions: centered or noncausal filtering as a primary result

stage1_gate.rule: Independent MATLAB/Simulink validation is allowed only if the causal primary predictor passes the decision-sufficiency kill criterion and retains at least 80 percent accuracy in the worst quartile of effective-mass diagnostic error.

target_population.policy: Continuous log-space sampling includes interpolation between and beyond the original six canonical classes; canonical labels are not used.
